about.storyTitle: From design to upkeep, under one roof.
about.storyBody1: Since 2017 we've designed, built and maintained pools in İzmir and the surrounding area. Every project starts by listening to what the site and the house need, and we plan the solution around that. Rather than off-the-shelf templates, we decide on the pool that best fits the space together with you.
about.storyBody2: We're a large, corporate team; with dedicated design, engineering, site and maintenance divisions, we have the capacity to run many projects at once. Our broad, expert staff keeps every stage — from design to handover — transparent and carefully planned, with all materials and work kept on record. After handover, our strong maintenance team stays with you for years to come.

faq.q: How long does building a pool in Çeşme or Alaçatı take?
faq.a: It depends on the pool's size, form and ground conditions. A standard villa pool is usually completed in 8–14 weeks after design approval. Projects with an infinity edge, a movable floor or complex automation take longer. We give you a clear schedule once the site survey is done.

faq.q: What is an infinity pool and which sites suit it?
faq.a: An infinity pool is one where the water spills invisibly over an edge and appears to merge with the horizon. It works best on sloped sites overlooking the sea or a valley. The overflowing water is collected in a balance tank below and continuously circulated, so it needs precise levelling and engineering.

faq.q: What is the difference between a gunite (sprayed concrete) pool and a fibreglass/prefabricated one?
faq.a: A gunite pool is built on site by spraying concrete over steel reinforcement; it can take any shape or size, lasts for decades and sits fully on the ground. Fibreglass/prefabricated pools are pre-moulded and limited in size. For durability and design freedom we build with gunite and reinforced concrete.

faq.q: Do you need a permit to build a pool in İzmir?
faq.a: Depending on the municipality and zoning status, a permit or notification may be required. We know the processes in Çeşme, Alaçatı and the surrounding districts, prepare the project in line with the relevant regulations and guide you through the paperwork and engineering calculations.

faq.q: What determines the cost of a pool?
faq.a: Cost is driven mostly by the pool's size and depth, the overflow type (infinity, deck-level, skimmer), the finish (ceramic, glass mosaic, travertine), ground conditions and the heating and automation equipment. After the site survey we provide a transparent, itemised quote.

faq.q: Can a pool be built on a sloped or view site?
faq.a: Yes. Sloped sites often give the strongest results for infinity edges and terraced pools. With soil surveys, retaining and engineering solutions we turn the slope into an advantage rather than a constraint.

faq.q: When in the year is it best to start building a pool?
faq.a: Because the season is long on the peninsula, late autumn, winter and early spring are the best windows for excavation and shell work. The noisy stages pass while the house is empty, and tiling and commissioning finish before the season opens. Projects that start in midsummer are usually prepared for the following season, so we suggest holding the decision and design conversations as early as you can.

faq.q: Can a pool be added later to a house with finished landscaping?
faq.a: Yes — a good share of our projects are exactly this. The deciding factor is site access: whether the garden gate and passage are wide enough for an excavator and a concrete pump, and if not, which excavation method replaces them. During the survey we mark in advance the areas to be lifted and relaid, the irrigation and electrical lines to be moved, and the trees to be protected. Restoring the disturbed landscaping is part of the handover.

faq.q: How is the pool's upkeep taken over once construction ends?
faq.a: Handover begins with commissioning: water balance is established, filtration and automation are set, and the use of the equipment is explained on site. From there we either take the pool onto a maintenance contract with our own team, or brief whoever you appoint on the system and its chemical targets. The reference values are the same either way: pH 7.2–7.6, free chlorine 1–3 ppm, total alkalinity 80–120 ppm.

faq.q: Can a salt chlorination system be installed at a seafront villa?
faq.a: It can. A salt chlorine generator converts salt into chlorine by electrolysis, disinfecting the water with a softer feel. Salt water is, however, harder on metal accessories, light housings and some natural stone finishes, so finishes, fixings and equipment must be selected with that in mind at the design stage. We make the call together during the site visit, based on the pool's form and how you plan to use it.

maintenance.title: Clarity of water, uninterrupted.
maintenance.intro: Regular pool maintenance for villas across İzmir — including Çeşme, Alaçatı, Ilıca, Seferihisar, Karaburun and Urla. A pool succeeds not on the day it is finished, but if it is still as clear as day one years later.

included.name: Chemical balance
included.desc: We measure pH, free chlorine, alkalinity and hardness on every visit and hold the water in balance — before any swing can harm skin or equipment.

included.name: Filtration & circulation
included.desc: Sand or cartridge filter cleaning, backwash, pump and valve checks. Proper circulation is the unseen engine of clarity.

included.name: Surface & floor cleaning
included.desc: Floor vacuuming by robot and by hand, wall brushing and waterline oil-band cleaning. Algae and scale are removed before they take hold.

included.name: Skimmer & line checks
included.desc: Cleaning of skimmer baskets, pump pre-filter and overflow channels — so leaves, insects and sediment never reach the system.

included.name: Equipment & automation
included.desc: Periodic checks of the heat pump, chlorination, dosing unit and lighting. Faults are caught quietly, before they grow.

included.name: Winterising & opening
included.desc: Protecting the water and draining the lines at season's end, then full recommissioning in spring. The pool passes winter unharmed.

maintenance.rhythmBody: From weekly checks to seasonal deep service — a maintenance calendar built around your pool's size and use. Every visit is reported and every reading logged. You enjoy the water; we take on the rest.
maintenance.ctaTitle: A maintenance plan for your pool.

faq.q: How often should a pool be serviced?
faq.a: Through the season (spring to autumn) weekly maintenance is ideal: measuring the water values, dosing, surface and floor cleaning and filter checks. Frequency may rise in heavy use or hot spells. In winter the pool is protected with a reduced but regular programme.

faq.q: What should the pool's pH and chlorine levels be?
faq.a: The ideal ranges are 7.2–7.6 for pH, 1–3 ppm for free chlorine and 80–120 ppm for total alkalinity. These values directly affect water clarity, skin and eye comfort and equipment life. We measure and rebalance them on every visit.

faq.q: How is a pool maintained in winter?
faq.a: When preparing a pool for winter the water level is set, the values are balanced, a winter chemical is applied and the plumbing is protected against freezing. The water is not fully drained; a cover and periodic checks ensure a healthy spring opening.

faq.q: Do you offer regular maintenance contracts for villas in Çeşme and Alaçatı?
faq.a: Yes. We offer seasonal and annual maintenance contracts for villas in Çeşme, Alaçatı, Ilıca and the surrounding districts. Our team visits at set intervals, measures and reports every value — so you enjoy the pool rather than manage it.

faq.q: Why does pool water turn cloudy or green?
faq.a: The most common causes are unbalanced pH/chlorine, weak filtration and algae growth. In hot weather chlorine is consumed quickly and algae multiply. With the right dosing, regular filter cleaning and, when needed, shock chlorination the water returns to clarity within a few days.

faq.q: How often should all the water be replaced?
faq.a: In a well-maintained pool a full water change is rarely needed — usually once every few years, or when the values can no longer be corrected chemically. Regular maintenance markedly reduces water use and cost.

faq.q: What should be done with a pool that will sit unused for a long time?
faq.a: The right approach is to leave the pool running rather than empty it. Before you leave, the readings are balanced, filtration time is set according to the location, and a cover is used. In hot weather, water left alone for weeks makes algae close to certain, so we continue periodic visits to test and dose while you are away. The pool is ready to use when you return.

faq.q: What is not included in a maintenance agreement?
faq.a: The agreement covers routine maintenance labour, testing and reporting, cleaning and regular checks. Items usually outside its scope are: replacing failed equipment and the cost of spare parts, surface or plumbing repair, fully draining and refilling the pool, and renovation work. When such items come up they are quoted separately, and nothing is carried out without your approval.

faq.q: What should an owner who maintains the pool themselves watch out for?
faq.a: The most common mistake is skipping the order: test before adding anything, correct pH before chlorine, and never mix two chemicals together. Dosing should be done while circulation is running, and always diluted. Noting filter pressure, backwashing according to that pressure, and storing chemicals in a cool, dry, locked place should not be neglected either.

faq.q: What happens if an equipment fault is found during a maintenance visit?
faq.a: The fault is diagnosed on site and noted in the report together with its cause. Minor interventions are completed during the same visit; if a part or more extensive work is needed, we share the options, the timeline and the cost in advance. In the meantime a temporary operating arrangement keeps the pool safe. The decision stays with you: no surprise invoices, no parts replaced without notice.

glance.title: The pool firm of the Çeşme peninsula.
glance.summary: Seçkin Havuzculuk (STC Royal A.Ş.) is a pool company working on villa and residential pools on İzmir's Çeşme peninsula since 2017. It builds pools from scratch (infinity, overflow and classic pools; gunite and reinforced concrete), renovates existing pools and provides contracted regular maintenance; it also supplies pool chemicals and equipment. Its service area covers Çeşme, Alaçatı, Ilıca, Seferihisar, Karaburun and Urla. The office is in Alaçatı and can be reached by phone and WhatsApp Monday to Saturday, 09:00–18:00.

faq.q: Which areas does Seçkin Havuzculuk serve?
faq.a: We work on İzmir's Çeşme peninsula: Çeşme, Alaçatı, Ilıca, Seferihisar, Karaburun and Urla. We plan each pool differently according to the area's climate, terrain and architecture; you can find area-specific details on our service-area pages.

faq.q: What services do you offer?
faq.a: Pool construction from scratch (infinity, overflow and classic pools), renovation of existing pools, contracted regular maintenance, season opening and winterizing. We also supply pool chemicals and filtration, lighting and cleaning equipment.

faq.q: How do the site visit and quote work?
faq.a: When you reach us by phone or WhatsApp, we schedule a free site visit. After assessing the land, the ground and how you plan to use the pool on site, we prepare a project-specific quote; the price depends on the pool's size, type and site conditions.

faq.q: Do you sell products online?
faq.a: No. Our product catalogue is for information only; we do not sell online. For information or to order a product, you can reach us by phone or WhatsApp.
